newsitem.title: UK: British Nov car registrations slip but up on year.
newsitem.headline: British Nov car registrations slip but up on year.

text.p: British car registrations fell by 5.4 percent in November to 135,342, but for the year so far the total number of sales remained ahead of the same 1995 period at 1,947,309 -- up 3.9 percent.

Industry body Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders Ltd (SMMT) said on Thursday that the monthly fall reflected lower new car registrations by both the private retail sector (down 6.1 percent) and the fleet or business market (down 4.9 percent).

SMMT chief executive Ernie Thompson was quoted in a statement as saying that although the monthly market was disappointing, cumulative sales showed that Britain's market was on course for over two million cars in the whole year.

Models produced by the European units of Ford Motor Co continued to lead the market although, unusually, in November the year's third best-selling Ford Mondeo recorded the highest number of registrations, at 6,451, while just 6,419 of the normally-top- selling Fiesta small car were registered in the period.

Overall in the year so far, however, Ford is not keeping pace with its 1995 performance in terms of market share, the SMMT data showed, and its share slipped to 19.62 percent from 21.34 in the period to November.

Meanwhile, Germany's Volkswagen AG is having a strong year, and has increased its market share in the first 11 months to 5.64 percent from 4.20 percent a year ago, but BMW-owned Rover continues to slide and saw its share reverse to 10.7 percent from 11.91 percent this time last year.
